Docker & Docker‑Compose – reproducible dev and production environments
GitHub Actions – CI linting and test automation
OpenTelemetry – end‑to‑end tracing for performance debugging
DVC – versioning of sample photo datasets and model checkpoints

title: TraceLLM: End‑to‑End Observability & Automatic Evaluation Platform for LLM Inference
summary: A lightweight SaaS‑style service that records every LLM call, stores prompts/responses with vector embeddings, streams OpenTelemetry traces, and automatically grades output with an LLM‑as‑judge. The data is visualized via a minimal React dashboard for latency, token usage and hallucination risk.
tech_stack: Python – core language for FastAPI and LangChain integration
FastAPI – lightweight, async HTTP service with automatic OpenAPI docs
LangChain – orchestrates LLM calls and self‑critique
OpenTelemetry Python SDK – captures traces, metrics, and logs without code changes
PostgreSQL + pgvector – persistent relational store with native vector search
Redis – short‑term cache for embeddings to keep latency low
Docker & Docker‑Compose – reproducible dev & deployment environment
GitHub Actions – CI/CD, linting, unit & integration tests
React (Vite) – simple SPA for dashboards (no heavy UI frameworks)

title: Personal Knowledge Navigator (PKN) – Multi‑Agent LLM Personal Assistant
summary: A privacy‑first web service that ingests a user’s notes, emails, and bookmarked web pages, builds a dynamic knowledge graph, and lets multi‑agent LLMs collaboratively summarize, link concepts, and answer natural‑language queries. Uses LangChain for retrieval, LangGraph for stateful reasoning, and CrewAI to orchestrate specialized agents.
tech_stack: FastAPI – lightweight HTTP API for the backend
LangChain – modular retrieval and prompt templates for document chunks
LangGraph – stateful graph‑based agent workflows (Node/Edge logic)
CrewAI – defines specialized agents (Ingestor, Summarizer, Querier) and task orchestration
Postgres with pgvector – persistent storage of raw documents and embeddings
Neo4j – graph database for entity‑level relationships and reasoning
Docker – containerised development & deployment
GitHub Actions – CI pipeline with linting, unit tests, and Docker build
React (optional) – simple UI for query input and result display

title: Adaptive Efficient Trainer (AET) for Large Models on Consumer GPUs
summary: A lightweight web service that profiles a user’s GPU, dataset, and model, then automatically configures mixed‑precision, gradient checkpointing, dynamic batch sizing, and gradient accumulation to maximize throughput while staying within memory limits.
tech_stack: FastAPI – lightweight HTTP API for profiling & optimizer endpoints
PyTorch – core DL framework for model loading and memory hooks
torch.cuda.amp – built‑in mixed‑precision support
torch.utils.checkpoint – gradient checkpointing implementation
psutil – system‑level GPU/CPU stats
Docker – reproducible container for the service
GitHub Actions – CI pipeline with MLflow tracking of benchmark runs
MLflow – experiment tracking for generated training configs
React (optional) – minimal UI for uploading model/dataset and displaying recommendations
